prompt: A flat layered paper-cut collage in a strict handcraft design system: everything is cut from colored cardstock and hanji paper with perfectly clean cut edges — NO outline of any kind on any piece: no bright edge line, no white edge, no dark contour line. Each object is built from two to five completely flat die-cut pieces layered ON THE OBJECT ITSELF — its own silhouette, a main color piece, one or two detail pieces and a highlight piece — the object is never placed on a base, platform, pedestal, plinth or pile of paper sheets; Every upper piece sits slightly RAISED above the piece beneath it, so along EVERY boundary where two different colors meet, the upper piece casts a soft narrow warm dark-brown shadow down onto the lower piece — a gentle embossed paper relief wherever two colors touch, and this relief shadow is the ONLY depth cue. Cut economy: every scissor cut is purposeful and confident — a shape that is straight in the real object is cut with a clean STRAIGHT edge, and curves appear ONLY where the real object is actually curved. No decorative wavy edges, no bumpy wobbly outlines, no gratuitous scalloping on untextured surfaces; a rectangular block is cut as a plain rectangle, though corners may be gently ROUNDED — softly rounding a corner is natural scissor work. Shapes stay simple and chunky, no detail finer than real scissors could cut. Scalloped repeat patterns for textures like straw or waves, cut big and loose. Strictly straight-on orthographic front view, zero perspective. No volume, no curvature, no folded paper, no sculpting. Real-scissors discipline: every piece is a shape that could actually be cut with scissors from a single sheet of colored paper. EACH PIECE IS EXACTLY ONE SOLID FLAT COLOR — no gradient, no shading, no airbrush, no painted detail inside a piece; every color change is a separate stacked paper piece, even a thin line is its own paper strip. ALL pieces share one identical fine colored-paper texture. All shadows are neutral warm dark-brown paper shadows, never colored. This is one DRAMATIC COMIC ACTION PANEL filling the ENTIRE image edge to edge (full-bleed, no border): bold dynamic composition, big flat paper speed-line strips, kid-friendly and funny, never scary. Cute, round, friendly Korean picture-book characters for 3-4 year olds: big round white paper eyes with dark pupils, small pink cheek circles, simple rounded shapes, never scary. The young bird looks down into the calm water and sees its reflection: a beautiful white swan. Surprised happy face, soft ripples. The young bird: a gangly pale-grey young swan made of flat paper pieces, side view facing LEFT — a long upright neck, a darker grey wing and tail, a pale belly, black feet, a brownish beak, a big round eye, pink cheek. Colour mood: soft, fresh spring picture-book pastels with low saturation — a pale soft blue sky, calm light sage greens, gentle pink blossoms; never lime, never saturated. IMPORTANT, read carefully: there is EXACTLY ONE animal in the whole picture — the young grey bird, standing alone on the grassy bank at the left, facing LEFT and bending its neck DOWN to look into the still water. NO swan on the bank, NO swan swimming on the water, NO second bird anywhere above the waterline. The ONLY white swan is the bird's own REFLECTION on the water surface directly below it: an upside-down mirror image where the grey bird's reflection has been replaced by a graceful snow-white swan with an orange beak and a long S-curved neck, slightly rippled and paler like a reflection. Above the water: one grey bird. Below the water: one white swan reflection. Nothing else. No text anywhere. Full-bleed illustration, no lime green.
